title: The Border
openLocation: Southeastern Eversong Woods, on Farstrider patrol near the Amani frontier.
transport: Thalassian horses for Sylvanas, Lor'themar, and the mounted patrol.
immediateObjective: Finish the troll sweep, dodge the Convocation budget session, and stay outdoors one more day.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Sylvanas; no head-hopping, nothing she could not perceive or infer

Jaina stays 'the mage', 'the human', or 'the prisoner' in Sylvanas's narration and thought for the whole chapter. Cyndia says the name aloud in Beat 7 and Sylvanas knows it from then on, but her own head does not use it (outline arc: 'Even then, Jaina is still only the mage, the human, or the prisoner inside Sylvanas's head').
No Jaina dialogue anywhere in this chapter
No trust or warmth between Sylvanas and Jaina
No plague, no leyline-corruption explanation, no proof beyond one stone humming wrong
Silvermoon is not shown directly; Convocation exists only as Sylvanas's avoidance

povKnowsAtOpen: Routine Amani pressure on the southeastern frontier
Ward network looks stable in every formal report
Farstriders keep files on powerful human mages near the border
Jaina Proudmoore is one of the names worth watching

That a human mage has already crossed the ward boundary

castKnowsLeavingChapter: Sylvanas has felt one ward-stone read wrong and seen it circled on Jaina's map; Jaina does not know this
Jaina is in Farstrider custody and must make her case to Sylvanas
Sylvanas knows the prisoner is Jaina Proudmoore
The breach is a serious interrogation, not a patrol annoyance

pov: She opens treating anything south of the wards as someone else's problem unless it touches her stones, roads, or riders.
She wants to finish the troll work, stay on her horse, and avoid the Convocation budget session.
A ward-stone hums wrong under her own palm. Then a runner reports a human mage inside the wards who says the leylines are wrong, and an easy patrol day becomes her problem.
By the end, the border mess belongs to her, and the prisoner is waiting in her own holding space.

beats: Before Sylvanas sees her, Jaina is just the human mage who ruined an easy day.
Sylvanas expects a polished Kirin Tor problem: spy, diplomat, or both.
What she finds instead is a road-worn young mage who looks exhausted, furious, and very far from court.
Even then, Jaina is still only the mage, the human, or the prisoner inside Sylvanas's head.

team.label: Partnership
beats: There is no partnership here. One woman is in custody, and the other decides how hard the door stays shut.
Jaina shifts from paperwork headache to the one person Sylvanas has to hear out.
The chapter ends on their first hard face-to-face with no warmth and no softening.

scenes.title: The Hunt
scenes.sceneFunction: Show Sylvanas in her element, have a ward-stone read wrong in her own hand, and bring the runner whose news confirms it.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Routine frontier work. Trolls are the only threat on the board. Sylvanas expects a slow day outdoors and dreads the budget session.
scenes.arcPressure: Test of her border-only frame: the stone and the runner make the south hers.
scenes.enrichment: Eversong's runestones are Highborne-built wards against Amani raids that also dampen non-elven magic (warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Eversong; wowpedia Eversong Woods); post-Second War Amani were hunted across Eversong, and Zul'jan lingered on the border (warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lightwood). Horse notes from thalassian-horses.md: sidestep then calm at ward vibration. Thalassian Pass (verifier-confirmed, warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thalassian_Pass): the mountain passage in the far southern Ghostlands linking Quel'Thalas to northern Lordaeron, gatehouse believed to be one of the elfgates. It is the Lordaeron-facing gate, which is where a human mage out of Dalaran would come in; it is not the troll-side border. The patrol works the southeastern Amani frontier and rides south to reach it.

beats.goal: Finish the troll sweep and take the last Amani axethrower as he breaks cover.
beats.conflict: Last raider bolts through thick ferns; she must judge footing, range and opening in a breath.

outcome.summary: Clean kill; the sweep is done and the patrol gets a breather.

newOnPageInformation: The sweep is finished and the patrol is clean
Sylvanas is most herself in the field, reading ground effortlessly
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Anything worse than trolls on the border
sensoryAnchors: troll blood in sweet Eversong air
beats.transitionIntent: sensory carry: the quiet after the kill, birdsong coming back, is the room she uses to stall

beats.goal: Stretch the patrol south on the pretext of checking ward-stones, then check the nearest stone herself, bare palm on the rune face.
beats.conflict: Lor'themar sees through the stall; the stone hums out of step with cold under the warmth, and she has no magister's vocabulary for it.

outcome.summary: She confirms something is off with the stone but cannot name it; Lor'themar files it under magister work and she rides on.

beats.decision: She keeps the cold stone to herself for the rest of the ride.

beats.verifierModification: Two fixes. (1) The outline says Sylvanas 'doubts even Cyndia expects a real threat from the south'. The planner had rewritten this as Sylvanas expecting no threat 'even from Cyndia's post', which is a different claim. Restored to the outline's meaning. It also plants Cyndia's name and post before the runner comes from there. (2) The budget session is now named in newOnPageInformation. It is part of the chapter goal, and Beat 5's split (Lor'themar takes the politicians) needs it set up first, but the plan only named it in Beat 5's interiority. Arc bullet 1 (south of the wards belongs to someone else) is anchored here as well, because no beat carried it before.

beats.goal: Hear the runner out and keep the patrol day intact.
beats.conflict: Runner brings news that cannot be waved off, and it matches the stone under her palm.

outcome.summary: Her easy day ends; the breach is a serious threat and the mage's claim echoes her own hand.

beats.transitionIntent: planted question: a mage who says the leylines are wrong, an hour after her own palm said the same; she has to see this herself
beats.verifierModification: Reconciled the ring conflict the planner flagged. In the runner's shorthand the mage is past the first (outer) ring. Cyndia's exact account in Beat 6 says she got through the outer ring and was stopped at the second. This matches the sample report shape on Cyndia's voice sheet ('She came over the second ring before dawn'). The runner and Cyndia must not contradict each other in prose.

beats.emotion: Irritation converting to command; glad of the excuse and irritated at being glad.
beats.dilemma: Hand the mage off, or ride south herself while Lor'themar takes the Convocation.
beats.decision: Splits the party: Lor'themar and patrol go north, she rides hard for the Pass with the runner and demands Cyndia's report on arrival.

scenes.title: The Prisoner
scenes.sceneFunction: A generic border arrest becomes a high-stakes problem that locks both women into the next chapter.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: A human mage is in a holding cell. No verified identity, no trusted warning. Sylvanas has felt one stone read wrong and arrives with the runner.
scenes.arcPressure: First hard face-to-face: she decides to hear the prisoner out, with no warmth.
scenes.enrichment: Cyndia: young-for-elf, auburn braid, green eyes, left-handed draw, scout-built; crisp, professional, volunteers good field observations before Ch 10 (characters/cyndia.md, cyndia-voice.md). Jaina: 23, blonde, blue-eyed, practical robes, scholar's hands with ink, calluses and frost-burns (characters/jaina.md). Antonidas is the Kirin Tor archmage and her mentor.

beats.goal: Get Cyndia's raw account of the arrest.
beats.conflict: The facts make the mage stranger, not clearer: she argued to stay and work instead of bolting.

outcome.summary: Report is close enough to Sylvanas's stone that she demands the gear and the prisoner at once.

newOnPageInformation: The mage got through the outer ring before dawn, was stopped at the second ring, and argued to stay and work instead of bolting
Stones read as if malfunctioning from something inside them

stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the human is arrogant, terrified, or right
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: she heads for the prisoner and stops at the lockdown rack on the way
beats.verifierModification: Ring detail now fits Beat 4 (outer ring crossed, stopped at the second). Weight set to short. Beats 6 and 7 are back-to-back information beats delivered through Cyndia. If both run long, the scene stalls before the door opens. Beat 6's pressure is Sylvanas pushing for the facts in order, and it should hand off quickly to the rack.

beats.conflict: The map is a puzzle: circled stones could be survey or target list, and one is the stone she checked this morning.

craftResearch.findings: Open on change, conflict or a character moving toward a goal, not on setup or waking. Feed worldbuilding in gradually instead of infodumping. Get the inciting incident into the first pages. Make the last line a hook into chapter two.
craftResearch.source: helpingwritersbecomeauthors.com/7-tips-for-opening-your-story-in-medias-res; dabblewriter.com/articles/write-first-chapter; goodreads author blog 'When In Media Res Overshoots the Mark'

craftResearch.findings: The scene is about who holds control and what non-compliance costs. The room itself (light, sound, confinement) applies pressure. Both parties want something.
Skip uneventful stretches with a clear time marker. Keep only travel that moves plot or reveals character, for example through conversation.
craftResearch.source: writing.codidact.com/posts/31131; mythicscribes.com community thread 'to and fro'

craftResearch.findings: Keep the first contact charged with conflict while planting one small humanizing detail. Quiet friction and body language can carry more than shouting.

pacing.notes: Tension: B1 medium-high, B2 medium, B3 low, B4 high, B5 medium, B6 medium, B7 medium-high, B8 high, B9 medium-high, B10 high. The curve dips after the opening action, spikes at the runner, releases on the ride, then climbs steadily to the cell door. No run of three high beats; B9 is a silent sequel beat that lets the tension breathe without dropping it. The two travel stretches (B3, B5) each do character work: Lor'themar's needling in B3, the split decision and interiority in B5. B5 is marked short; the ride to the Pass should be a time jump carried by the sensory gradient rather than played in full. Risk: B6 and B7 are consecutive information beats through Cyndia. B6 is marked short to keep the scene moving.

structure.notes: Opening drops into the last kill of a sweep, so it starts mid-action. The inciting disturbance (the stone) arrives in B2. The mid-chapter turn lands at B4-B5 (40-50%), and B7's circled stone gives a second turn. Closing line 'Start talking' leaves the interrogation open. Scene/sequel split is 6/4, which is about right for a chapter that is half field action and half confrontation. Only two scenes, which is fixed by the outline. Variety comes from beat weight instead: S1 runs long-short-medium, S2 runs short-medium-medium.

character.notes: Sylvanas drives every beat: she kills, stalls, checks, keeps silent, splits the party, demands, inspects, opens the door, reads, takes the floor. No passive run. Supporting cast are distinct: Lor'themar needles and takes the politics, the runner carries the news, Cyndia supplies facts in order, the rangers wait. Every arc bullet now lands (see arcLandingMap). POV guards were added on B8 (her inference about the prisoner's fury) and B10 (file facts vs. her own picture). The constraint on Jaina's name was corrected to match the outline: Sylvanas does not think of her as Jaina even after hearing the name.

transitions.notes: All 10 intents present and causally sound. Labels normalized to the standard types. B8 was retyped from sensory carry to emotional carryover. B5 lands in S2's opening state (arrival, report demanded). B10 hands off to Chapter 2's Jaina POV, which must not replay the line.

continuity.notes: Chapter 1, so there is no memory to check against and no contradictions with prior chapters. Within the chapter, the first/second ring conflict between B4 and B6 is reconciled: past the outer ring, stopped at the second. The 'troll-side Pass' worry is resolved: the canon Thalassian Pass is the Lordaeron-facing gate in southern Ghostlands, and the patrol rides south to it. The stone thread is tracked through B2, B4, B7 and B9 via intraChapterEcho. Timeline holds: the mage crossed before dawn, the sweep is in the morning, the B7 reference to 'this morning' fits, and the prisoner sits for hours before Chapter 2.
